title: Pressure vessel with hemispherical heads, equal thickness (axisymmetric)
description:
Steel pressure vessel: a cylindrical shell closed by two hemispherical heads, under internal pressure. Axisymmetric problem.
Geometry file (STEP): the meridional section of the vessel wall, drawn in the xy-plane: x is the radius (x >= 0, axis of revolution x = 0) and y is the axial coordinate z, with z = 0 at mid-length.
Cylinder: inner radius 250 mm, wall thickness 20 mm, straight length 1000 mm between the head junctions (z from -500 mm to 500 mm). The hemispherical heads have inner radius 250 mm and the same wall thickness 20 mm; inside and outside surfaces are tangent-continuous at the junctions.
Material: steel, linear elastic and isotropic, E = 200 GPa, Poisson's ratio 0.3.
Load: internal pressure 5 MPa on every inner surface (cylinder and heads). No other loads; the vessel is free (self-equilibrated): constrain only the axial rigid-body translation, without stressing the vessel.
Analysis: linear static, small displacements, axisymmetric.
Report (in an axisymmetric model, x = r and y = z):
  hoop_stress_mid: the hoop (circumferential) stress at the inner surface at mid-length, the point (r, z) = (250 mm, 0) [Pa];
  peak_von_mises: the maximum von Mises stress anywhere in the vessel wall [Pa].
